assertions: Fresh browser shows genuine empty host; service worker enables isolation without server headers.
Workspace and note created through UI receive real durable host receipts.
Production startup theme observer cannot override explicit Light or Dark after an OS preference change.
Phone fragment survives initial isolation reload, clears from URL, remains memory-only, and does not auto-join.
Observed host stages reach the production UI through the real worker before joining completes.
Explicit phone Join completes an authenticated peer exchange and imports the real note.
Notes edited from each production UI converge across isolated real browser hosts.
Phone material fits viewport, picker is on demand, and capture keeps its original workspace across navigation.
Peer update preserves unsaved editor; explicit reconciliation saves a new revision.
Offline browser-process restart opens cached application and retained identity/work; offline save succeeds.
Foreground reconnection exchanges the offline edit with the paired browser.
Service-worker caches contain application assets only; no fragment, pairing ticket, or workspace records.
Production browser bundle contains no native bridge or native speech/scanner calls.
scope: Built production UI with real BrowserHost, Turso OPFS and Iroh peers; headers-free static /shared-workspace/ origin.
limits: Desktop Chromium with phone viewport; no physical iPhone result.
Browser speech adapter tested separately; no microphone recognition claim.
No public deployment from this test.
